I'll translate the recipe of one of our most popular tv-chefs. He likes to cook traditionally, and generally his recipes are very good, but a little bit more complicated than how everyone's grandma does it. Feel free to improvise, everyone does.

4 persons, +-3 hours

Ingrediënts

  • 1 kg beef (shank)
  • 2 big onions
  • 1 bottle of dark/amber beer (Like a nice abbey amber ale)
  • Fresh thyme
  • 1 clove
  • 2 bay leaves
  • 1 slice of brown bread
  • 2 spoons of strong mustard (not that sweet american stuff)
  • natural vinegar
  • butter
  • pepper
  • salt
  • 1 kg potatoes

Preparation

Carbonade:

  • Peel the onions and slice them.
  • Heat a large casserole, melt a knob of butter. Fry the onions over medium heat. Don't let the onions brown.
  • Heat a frying pan over medium heat, melt a knob of butter.
  • Sear the pieces of meat in the frying pan until they are golden brown tan. Season the meat during cooking with some ground pepper and a pinch of salt.
  • Tip: A large amount of meat is best baked in several batches. If your skillet is too full, the meat will be cooked instead of fried.
  • Add the pieces of meat in the stew with the onions. Keep the frying pan as is (with the gravy etc.) and pour the beer in. Stir the meat pan frequently, knocking loose the grease etc. on the sides while the beer is brought to boiling point.
  • Tip: Feel free to use a little more beer than indicated.
  • Once the beer is boiling, pour it into the stew.
  • Bind a few bay leaves and a few sprigs of fresh thyme together with a little kitchen twine. Add to the stew.
  • Add the clove
  • Spread mustard generously over the slice of brown bread. Add the slice to the stew, mustard side down.
  • Let the pot simmer over low heat for half an hour to three hours. The lid does not need to be on. The amount of time depends on the quality of the meat. Stir occasionally check regularily whether the meat is sufficiently cooked. (Some people go to the point where the meat is nearly falling apart, you're gonna want it nice and soft.)
  • When the stew sauce has reached the desired thickness, place the lid on the stew.
  • When ready: add a dash of vinegar and stir everything.
  • Taste and season with ground pepper and salt.

The fries: this is some kind of special preparation. I've never seen anyone do it this way. Y'all know how to make fries so you can skip this part.

  • Peel the potatoes and cut by hand into uniform fries. They need not be too thin, the perfect Belgian frite is 13 mm thick.
  • Wash the fries to rinse the starch off.
  • Heat the oil/fat (preferably animal fat) at 140°C/285°F.
  • Bake the fries a first time, but don't let them change color. (You're poaching the pieces.)
  • Let the fries cool down in a bowl lined with paper towels.
  • Heat the oil/fat to 180°C/356 °F.
  • Fry the frites untils golden and crisp
  • Pour the chips back in a dish with paper towels so they can drain life. Sprinkle with some salt.

Serve

Serve a portion of stew with fries and a large spoonful of mayonnaise.

So, to give you back, here is a recipe for a dish that I love. I am translating the recipes from here and here.

For the rice This is an easy one. Just putting it here for completeness.

  • 2 1/2 tablespoons of butter or 2 tablespoons of olive oil
  • 1 chopped onion
  • 1 garlic clove
  • 2 1/2 cup of white rice (basmati works better)
  • 750 ml of water

  • 2 teaspoons of salt

  • Heat the butter (or olive oil) and throw the onions until it is soft.

  • Add the garlic and then the rice and fry it.
  • Add the water and salt until cooked.

Farofa de dendê

  • Half a cup (about 120ml) of dendê oil
  • 4 tablespoons (about 40g) of chopped onions
  • 2 cups of toasted cassava flour

  • Half a teaspoon of salt.

  • Put the oil in a pan over medium heat and let it get hot.

  • Add the onions and fry it until soft.
  • Slowly add the flour, always mixing with a wooden spoon.
  • Let it fry until the flour has absorbed all the oil
  • Add salt and mix.
  • Serve hot.

Moqueca Baiana

  • 700g of a mix of a firm fish sliced in pieces, crab meat and shrimp
  • 4 tablespoons of lemon juice
  • 3 chopped cloves of garlic
  • 1 teaspoon of salt
  • 1 teaspoon of grounded black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons of dendê oil
  • 1 onion, sliced in rings
  • 1 yellow bell pepper, without the seeds, sliced in rings
  • 1 orange or red bell pepper,without the seeds, sliced in rings
  • 1 tablespoon of chopped and dried chilli peppers
  • 3 sliced tomatoes
  • 1 chopped tomato
  • Half a cup of chopped chives
  • Half a cup of chopped coriander

  • 400g of coconut milk

  • Mix the fish and seafood with the lemon juice, garlic, half the salt and black pepper. Let it rest for a while.

  • Fry the onions in the dendê oil in medium heat until soft.
  • Add the chilli pepper and the bell peppers.
  • Add the tomatoes and chive.
  • Reduce the heat and let it cook for 5 minutes.
  • Add the rest of the salt, black pepper and the coriander.
  • Take out half out of the pan and put in a dish. With the half that is left, make it cover all the bottom of the pan.
  • Add the fish and seafood and use the half in the dish to cover it all.
  • Add the coconut milk on top.
  • Let it boil, then reduce the heat and let it cook, with the lid on, for 15 minutes, mixing every now and then.
  • Check the spices, add more coriander if you wish, or pepper, and serve hot.

This fish stew is eaten with the rice and farofa as side dishes. Have fun!

Just a tip: dendê oil may cause some stomach problems if you are not used to it, so make it in a Saturday to give you time to recover until Monday.
